name: REGENT (Retrieval-Augmented Generalist Agent)
venue: ICLR 2025 (Oral); preprint arXiv:2412.04759 (Dec 2024). Also presented at NeurIPS 2024 Workshops on Adaptive Foundation Models (AFM) and Open World Agents (OWA).
authors_affiliation: Kaustubh Sridhar, Souradeep Dutta, Dinesh Jayaraman, Insup Lee. Primary affiliation: University of Pennsylvania (Souradeep Dutta also University of British Columbia).
code_url: https://github.com/regent-research/regent (Apache-2.0; HuggingFace models/data at https://huggingface.co/regent-research; OpenReview https://openreview.net/forum?id=NxyfSW6mLK)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper artifact repo at https://github.com/regent-research/regent; not a continuously-updated leaderboard/paper-list)
task_domain: Decision-making / sequential control: generalist agents for robotics (Metaworld, Mujoco) and game-playing (Atari, BabyAI, ProcGen) environments. Embodied/RL control rather than text QA.
problem_setting: Pre-train a single small generalist policy on offline expert demonstration datasets from K training environments (across heterogeneous observation/action modalities), then deploy directly in held-out UNSEEN environments via in-context learning with only a few expert demonstrations and NO finetuning. Each environment is an MDP; state and action spaces of unseen environments are assumed known. Setting is offline pre-training plus interactive deployment (online rollouts in the environment); single-agent; expert demonstrations available for retrieval. The agent acts step-by-step, retrieving from the few demonstrations provided in the new environment.
what_is_retrieved: (state, previous-reward, action) tuples drawn from expert demonstration trajectories. In R&P the nearest demonstration state's action is replayed; in REGENT the n nearest tuples form the in-context demonstrations for the transformer.
retrieval_grounding: Static external corpus of expert demonstrations: a frozen set of demonstration trajectories (a designated retrieval subset of pre-training environment datasets during training; the few provided demos in the unseen environment at deployment). Not a growing/episodic agent-written memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k (top-n) similarity ranking: retrieve the n=19 nearest states (plus the single nearest for the R&P branch). No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size retrieval; k is a fixed hyperparameter.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse] (no Revise, no Retain). REGENT Retrieves nearest (state,reward,action) tuples and Reuses them (R&P replays the nearest action; the transformer adapts/interpolates). It does not Revise retrieved cases or Retain new cases into the store.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself as retrieval-augmented generation / semi-parametric policy and in-context learning (inspired by RAG/RETRO/REALM for language models); it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or frame itself as case-based reasoning.
retrieval_unit: (state, reward, action) tuple. The query/key is the state (image embedding or proprioceptive vector); each retrieved unit is a single transition tuple (state, previous reward, action) from a demonstration.
index_source: Offline-induced static store. The retrievable set is built from expert demonstration datasets: during pre-training a randomly chosen subset of demonstrations per environment is designated as the retrieval set; at deployment the handful of provided demonstrations in the unseen environment. The store is frozen (does not grow during deployment).
index_structure_topology: Flat similarity index over state vectors. In the JAT/Gato setting, FAISS-style approximate similarity-search indices over L2 state embeddings; in the ProcGen setting, a naive (GPU-parallelized) nearest-image search using SSIM distance. No graph/hierarchy.
retriever_type: Dense / nearest-neighbor (non-learned). L2 nearest-neighbor over ResNet18-ImageNet image embeddings or raw proprioceptive vectors (JAT/Gato setting); SSIM-distance nearest-image search over raw images (ProcGen setting). Off-the-shelf similarity search (FAISS), not a learned retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf, fixed similarity). The retriever is a fixed nearest-neighbor search using L2 distance (JAT/Gato) or SSIM distance (ProcGen) over frozen embeddings (ResNet18 trained only on ImageNet, or raw observations). The retriever is not trained or optimized; only the downstream transformer policy is trained.
query_construction: The raw current/query state is used directly as the query. Images are embedded with a frozen off-the-shelf ResNet18 (ImageNet) into 512-d vectors (JAT/Gato); proprioceptive vectors are used unmodified; ProcGen images are used directly with SSIM. No query decomposition, expansion, or thought-conditioning.
query_granularity: Step/state-level: retrieval is performed at every timestep using the current query state (one retrieval per environment step during the rollout).
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / per-step: retrieval is triggered at every timestep of the rollout (fixed schedule, once per state).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval occurs deterministically at every environment step for the current query state. No confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger.
reranking: No reranking stage. Retrieved states are simply ordered by closeness (L2 or SSIM distance) to the query, with the closest placed first in the context.
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond ordering. Retrieved (state,reward,action) tuples are placed in the context in order of closeness to the query (closest first); distances are normalized and clipped to [0,1]. No decomposition, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression. (Constraint applied at training time: retrieved states for a query may not come from the same demonstration as the query.)
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/documents; retrieved units are state-action-reward tuples).
index_content_separation: N/A (no separate lightweight-index-then-content scheme; the index keys are the state embeddings and the loaded content is the corresponding (state,reward,action) tuple).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index/protocol; this is a control policy, not a tool-use agent).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools / no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt/context augmentation plus retrieve-and-play action injection. The n=19 retrieved (state,reward,action) tuples are placed in the transformer's context (in-context demonstrations) along with the query state and previous reward; the transformer's action prediction is then combined with the nearest retrieved action via a distance-weighted interpolation. Retrieval also acts as a training signal: REGENT is pre-trained on sequences of queries and retrieved neighbors.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-then-act (no explicit planner or tree search). At each step the agent retrieves nearest neighbors, feeds them as in-context demonstrations to the transformer, and produces a single action via interpolation between the retrieve-and-play (R&P) action and the parametric transformer output: pi_REGENT = e^{-lambda*d}*pi_R&P + (1-e^{-lambda*d})*sigma(pi_theta), where d is the (normalized, clipped) distance from the query state to the closest retrieved state.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step (per environment action / per state): one retrieval and one interpolated action prediction per timestep of the rollout. No CoT/token-level interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: Distance-weighted interpolation between verbatim retrieve-and-play (closest retrieved action) and the parametric transformer policy, with the transformer trained to predict the residual to the R&P action. When the query state is very close to the nearest retrieved state, REGENT essentially replays the retrieved action; as distance grows, the parametric policy takes precedence. This is the key in-context adaptation mechanism (no LLM-prompted case rewriting, no RL reuse-finetuning).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw transition tuples: encoded (state, previous-reward, action) tuples placed in the transformer context as in-context demonstrations (image embeddings / proprioceptive vectors / discrete-token observations, plus reward and action). No distilled strategy or free-text workflow; surface form is the raw retrieved transitions.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw demonstration transitions (low abstraction): individual (state, reward, action) tuples from expert trajectories, not distilled strategies, guidelines, skills, or workflows.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retrieval-augmented pre-training plus distance-weighted interpolation. The transformer is trained on sequences of queries and retrieved neighbors (so it learns to use possibly-imperfect retrieved context), and the e^{-lambda*d} weighting downweights the R&P action and relies more on the parametric policy when the nearest retrieved state is far (potentially less reliable). Distances are normalized and clipped to [0,1]; sticky-action stochasticity is added at deployment to stress-test true generalization. No explicit relevance evaluator or self-reflection module.
memory_type: none (static demonstration store only). The retrievable set is a fixed corpus of expert demonstrations; there is no episodic/skill/workflow memory written by the agent.
write_back: False. The agent never writes new experiences/cases/skills back into the retrievable store; the demonstration set is fixed.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store does not grow during deployment; it is the fixed set of provided demonstrations in the unseen environment.
failure_experience_usage: Not applicable / success-only. The retrievable store is composed of expert demonstrations (generated by an expert policy maximizing return); failed/negative experiences are not stored or retrieved.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (store is frozen; entries are never mutated, merged, refined, or pruned after construction).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed similarity top-k (L2 or SSIM nearest neighbors), not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. Only the downstream transformer action policy is trained (the retriever and the R&P selection rule are fixed).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent, single-policy; the demonstration store is private to the deployed agent. No cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: JAT/Gato setting: Metaworld (45 training + 5 unseen), Mujoco (9 training + 2 unseen embodiments), Atari (52 training + 5 unseen), BabyAI (39 training). ProcGen setting (adapted from MTT): 12 training environments, 5 held-out unseen environments, plus unseen levels of training environments (e.g., bigfish, maze). Total pre-training: ~14.5M transitions (JAT/Gato) and ~12M transitions (ProcGen).
benchmark_family: embodied/robotics control (Metaworld, Mujoco) and decision-RL game-playing (Atari, BabyAI, ProcGen). Gato/JAT-style multi-environment generalist-agent suites; not QA/web/tool/code benchmarks.
baselines: JAT/Gato setting: JAT/Gato (apples-to-apples, same data as REGENT); JAT/Gato (All Data, 5x Atari / 10x other data); JAT/Gato + RAG at inference (same retrieval as REGENT); fully-finetuned and PEFT (IA3) variants of both JAT/Gato models; train-from-scratch behavior cloning; DRIL (imitation learning); plus the R&P 1-nearest-neighbor baseline. ProcGen setting: MTT (Multi-Trajectory Transformer, Meta; ~3x parameters, ~10x more pre-training levels/data). Referenced large agents include Gato (1.2B params), MGDT (Multi-Game Decision Transformer, requires 1M transitions).
key_metrics: Normalized return = (total return - random return) / (expert return - random return), reported against number of demonstrations (25/50/75/100 for Metaworld/Atari; 2/4/8/12/16/20 for ProcGen) or number of demonstration states (>=10k/15k/20k/25k for Atari). Aggregate training-environment performance reported via IQM and mean normalized return. Also reports parameter count and pre-training datapoint count as efficiency metrics.
headline_result: REGENT generalizes to unseen robotics and game-playing environments via retrieval augmentation + in-context learning with NO finetuning, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art generalist agents (JAT/Gato including its All Data variant and finetuned/PEFT variants in the JAT/Gato setting; MTT in the ProcGen setting) while using up to 3x fewer parameters (REGENT 138.6M vs JAT 192.7M in JAT/Gato; 116M vs MTT 310M in ProcGen) and up to an order-of-magnitude fewer pre-training datapoints. Notably, the simple R&P 1-nearest-neighbor baseline alone (no pre-training, no neural net) already matches or beats the SOTA generalist agents.
ablations: (1) Interpolation ablation: WITHOUT the distance-weighted interpolation between R&P and the transformer, REGENT fails to generalize (performs like a random agent) on unseen environments -- interpolation is identified as key. (2) Context size/length: larger context improves performance but saturates quickly. (3) Context order: ordering retrieved states by closeness (closest first) is important, especially when unseen environments differ markedly from pre-training (e.g., Atari). (4) Distance metric: L2 outperforms cosine distance (JAT/Gato). (5) Inference-time / runtime ablations also reported. (6) R&P vs REGENT: R&P is a strong baseline but REGENT consistently improves on it.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task performance (normalized return) is reported; there are no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) decoupled from task success.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (normalized return / aggregate IQM). Qualitative process analysis is provided (visualizing inputs/outputs at key states in atari-pong and metaworld-bin-picking showing when REGENT matches vs improves on R&P), but no quantitative step-wise retrieval/process accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a central claim: up to 3x fewer parameters (138.6M vs 192.7M JAT; 116M vs 310M MTT) and up to ~10x fewer pre-training datapoints (14.5M vs 5-10x more for JAT All Data; ProcGen uses <=1565 levels vs 10k for MTT). Adapts to new Atari games with as little as ~10k transitions and no finetuning, vs MGDT needing 1M transitions. FAISS similarity indices and GPU-parallelized SSIM speed up retrieval; inference runtimes discussed in appendix. No per-call API cost (not an LLM agent).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k context: n=19 retrieved (state,reward,action) tuples plus the query state (and previous reward), giving n+1=20 action predictions during training. Context size is a fixed hyperparameter (ablated; larger helps but saturates). Not adaptive or precision-driven.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (primary research paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmark suites; not a new benchmark paper). Data is reused/subsetted from the open-source JAT dataset (100k transitions x 145 training environments = 14.5M) and PPO-generated ProcGen rollouts (20 rollouts x 12 environments to reach 1M each = 12M).
builds_on: JAT (open-source Gato reproduction, HuggingFace) -- REGENT adapts JAT's architecture and training recipe in the JAT/Gato setting and subsets the JAT dataset; Gato (DeepMind) generalist agent; MTT (Multi-Trajectory Transformer, Meta) for the ProcGen setting and in-context comparison; retrieval-augmented language modeling (RAG (Lewis et al.), RETRO, REALM) as inspiration for semi-parametric retrieval augmentation; nearest-neighbor few-shot learning; theoretical analysis adapted from Sridhar et al. (sub-optimality bound, MixedReLU activation).
contrasts_with: Large monolithic generalist agents that scale parameters/data (Gato, JAT, RoboCat, Multi-Game Decision Transformer, RT-series, Octo, OpenVLA, Mobility VLA, BAKU, RoboAgent) which struggle to generalize to unseen environments without many finetuning transitions; MTT (positioned against as the only other in-context-adaptable agent, but with ~3x params and ~10x data); in-context RL methods that only adapt to new tasks WITHIN the same environment (Algorithm Distillation, Decision-Pretrained Transformer, Prompt Decision Transformer); plain RAG-at-inference applied to a non-retrieval-pretrained policy (JAT/Gato + RAG), which REGENT outperforms.
lineage: Group F (decision-making / memory / RL). A semi-parametric, retrieval-augmented in-context generalist agent for sequential decision-making: retrieves (state,reward,action) tuples and interpolates a retrieve-and-play 1-NN policy with a transformer, porting RAG-style retrieval augmentation from language modeling into multi-environment RL control for fast adaptation to unseen environments without finetuning.
